decisions.decision: D-01: Input Gain is now a pre-clamp float multiply on BOTH paths (plugin and standalone), applied to the host buffer / WAV samples BEFORE the int16 boundary clamp.
decisions.rationale: Gives the user real headroom: knob below unity attenuates before clip rather than scaling an already-clipped result.

decisions.decision: D-02: Input Gain parameter range internal float is 0.0..16.0 (+24 dB drive). Standalone slider widened to expose this range in-phase; plugin host-param surface still deferred to Phase 24 / PLUG-28.
decisions.rationale: User chose aggressive +24 dB ceiling to turn sat_s16 into a deliberate saturator -- North Star 'fixed-point quirks ARE the product.' UAT confirmed audible character is right.

decisions.decision: D-03: spu94_set_input_gain engine register is pinned at 0x7FFF on BOTH paths (uniformed during UAT correction from plugin-only).
decisions.rationale: Original split (standalone using engine register, plugin pre-clamp) overflowed int16_t once the atomic range widened to 0.0..16.0 -- audibly: quieter past 1.0 then silent. Uniform pinning eliminates the wrap.

decisions.decision: Bit corruption / int16 wrap is a recurring failure mode in this codebase.
decisions.rationale: Same shape of bug appeared in v1.5 register shadows (commit e2e8f57, 2026-05-05) and in Phase 23 Plan 02's first revision. Any cast 'float -> int16_t' with values that can exceed +/-32767 must either clamp first or use a wider integer type. Worth flagging at design-review time on any new register/parameter wiring.

context_notes: Phase 23 closeout was clean but bumpy mid-execution: the planner's D-03 decision (standalone keeps engine-register gain) plus the slider exposure deferral combined to make the audible behavior unreachable in any UI -- discovered during UAT when Anthony first swept past 1.0 and heard the int16 wrap evaporate the signal. Recovered with a single post-UAT commit (7e9bc82) that uniformed the register policy and widened the standalone slider. Lesson worth keeping: when a phase touches an audible parameter range, the GUI surface that exposes the range is part of the UAT contract -- deferring slider widening to a 'GUI phase' produces a phase that can't actually be heard. Anthony's UAT approval ("This sounds great btw. listening now") followed by an unprompted creative spitball on the Bit Corrupt effect and PSX sampler product direction -- both logged to memory + STATE deferred ideas, both are post-SPU-94 product moves.
